questions.q: How is a toast notification actually displayed from an LWC component?
options: By calling a global function named showToast()
By creating a ShowToastEvent and dispatching it with this.dispatchEvent(...), exactly like any other event
By setting a property named toastMessage directly on the component
Toasts can only be triggered from Apex, never from LWC
questions.explain: ShowToastEvent is a CustomEvent subclass -- it's created with `new ShowToastEvent({...})` and dispatched with this.dispatchEvent(...), the same mechanism used for any other event.

questions.q: Which toast variant is intended specifically to signal that an action failed?
options: info
warning
error
success
questions.explain: The error variant (red, with an error icon) specifically signals that an action failed. success signals it completed, warning signals something needs attention without being a failure, and info is the general-purpose default.

questions.q: What does dropping a `<lightning-messages></lightning-messages>` element inside a `lightning-record-edit-form` do?
options: It manually dispatches a ShowToastEvent whenever the form is submitted
It automatically displays any error the form encounters when saving, with no JavaScript required
It validates the form's fields before the user can submit
It replaces the need for the onsuccess and onerror attributes on the form
questions.explain: lightning-messages is a declarative component that automatically surfaces errors from its surrounding record form -- it requires no JavaScript error-handling code to display them.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a shared helper function (like the `reduceError` example) for extracting an error's message?
options: Because Apex and LDS errors don't always have exactly the same shape, so a shared helper avoids repeating fragile, inconsistent error-parsing logic across components
Because error.body.message is deprecated and no longer works in any case
Because a helper function is required by the LWC compiler for any try/catch block
Because toasts cannot display a message longer than 10 characters without a helper
questions.explain: Different error sources don't guarantee identical shapes, so a shared helper that checks a few known shapes (an array of errors, a single error.body.message, or a plain error.message) keeps error display consistent across a project.

questions.q: When is ShowToastEvent the standard mechanism to reach for, versus lightning-messages?
options: ShowToastEvent is only for success cases; lightning-messages is only for error cases
For imperative Apex or LDS JavaScript calls, where there's no form component already managing error display -- lightning-messages fits specifically inside a record-edit-form
They are fully interchangeable with no difference in when to use each
lightning-messages replaces ShowToastEvent entirely in current API versions
questions.explain: lightning-messages is the lower-effort, declarative option specifically for errors inside a record form. For imperative JavaScript calls (Apex or LDS), there's no form already managing error display, so ShowToastEvent is the standard way to surface feedback.
